 Al Shabab host Al Ahli at SHG Arena in Riyadh in the Saudi Pro League, with Thomas Letsch's side looking to arrest a run of inconsistent results against a visiting team that arrives in strong form.
 Al Shabab sit 12th in the table and have struggled for consistency this season. They beat Al-Taawoun 3-0 not long ago but have also dropped points against Al-Faisaly and lost to Al Kholood, reflecting a squad that can produce but has not yet found a reliable rhythm.
 Al Ahli, coached by Marino Pusic, are a different proposition right now. They have won all five of their last matches across the Saudi Pro League and AFC Champions League Elite, scoring 16 goals in the process. That kind of momentum is difficult to stop.
 Ivan Toney leads the scoring charts in the Saudi Pro League this season with 13 goals in 14 appearances. His availability for this fixture has been in question following a court appearance in London earlier this week, with reports indicating Al Ahli's management have been working to facilitate his return to Riyadh in time to face Al Shabab.
 The two clubs have met four times in recent seasons, and Al Ahli have the better of the recent record. Their last meeting at SHG Arena ended 2-5 to the visitors in February 2026, a result that underlines just how much ground Al Shabab need to make up.

 How to watch on the Big Screen
 Watching on your phone or laptop is fine, but live sports belongs on the big screen. Here is how to get the VPN working on your TV:
 Smart TVs & Fire Stick: Most Android-based TVs and devices like the Amazon Fire TV Stick or Google Chromecast with Google TV have native VPN apps. Simply search for your VPN provider in the app store on your TV, log in, and connect just like you would on your phone.
